source: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Section 2.1 History (rec 1: characteristics and duration, associated features, CV risk factors) and Table 3. Not covered: Table 3 'Severity' row (aortic-syndrome cue) and physical exam (Sec 2.2).

items.label: Nature of the pain
items.description: Clinician asks what the pain feels like (pressure, tightness, sharp, burning).
example_questions: What does the pain feel like?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Sec 2.1 (e377) and Table 3 'Nature' (e378)
items.guideline_quote: Anginal symptoms are perceived as retrosternal chest discomfort (eg, pain, discomfort, heaviness, tightness, pressure, constriction, squeezing)
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text. ADDED after guideline check; not in the original report list.

items.label: Onset and duration
items.description: Clinician establishes when the pain started, how it began and how long it lasts.
example_questions: Did it come on suddenly or gradually?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Onset and duration' (e378)
items.guideline_quote: Anginal symptoms gradually build in intensity over a few minutes.
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Location and radiation
items.description: Clinician asks where the pain is and whether it spreads to the arm, jaw, neck or back.
example_questions: Does it travel to your arm or jaw?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Location and radiation' (e378); Sec 2.1 supportive text (e377)
items.guideline_quote: characteristic radiation (eg, left arm, neck, jaw)
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Precipitating factors (exertion)
items.description: Clinician asks whether the pain is brought on by exertion or emotional stress, or happens at rest.
example_questions: Does it happen when you walk or climb stairs?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Precipitating factors' (e378)
items.guideline_quote: Physical exercise or emotional stress are common triggers of anginal symptoms.
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Relieving factors
items.description: Clinician asks what makes the pain better (rest, medication).
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Relieving factors' (e378); Sec 1.4.2 supportive text (e376)
items.guideline_quote: Relief with nitroglycerin is not necessarily diagnostic of myocardial ischemia and should not be used as a diagnostic criterion.
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text. ADDED after guideline check; not in the original report list.

items.label: Shortness of breath
items.description: Clinician asks about shortness of breath with the pain.
example_questions: Are you short of breath when this happens?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Associated symptoms' (e378)
items.guideline_quote: Common symptoms associated with myocardial ischemia include, but are not limited to, dyspnea, palpitations, diaphoresis, lightheadedness, presyncope or syncope
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Sweating
items.description: Clinician asks about sweating (diaphoresis) with the pain.
example_questions: Do you break out in a sweat when it happens?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Associated symptoms' (e378)
items.guideline_quote: dyspnea, palpitations, diaphoresis, lightheadedness, presyncope or syncope
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Fainting or lightheadedness
items.description: Clinician asks about fainting, near-fainting or lightheadedness.
example_questions: Have you passed out or felt like you might?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Table 3 'Associated symptoms' (e378); Sec 2.1 supportive text (e377)
items.guideline_quote: Associated symptoms such as shortness of breath, nausea or vomiting, lightheadedness, confusion, presyncope or syncope... are more frequent among patients with diabetes, women, and the elderly.

items.label: Cardiovascular risk factors
items.description: Clinician asks about cardiac risk factors: smoking, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol.
example_questions: Any history of high blood pressure, diabetes or high cholesterol?

items.guideline_quote: a focused history that includes ... cardiovascular risk factor assessment should be obtained
items.verification_note: Matched against the guideline text (provided PDF) by Claude, not clinician-reviewed. 'VERIFIED' = the element appears in the cited guideline text.

items.label: Family history
items.description: Clinician asks about heart disease in close relatives.
example_questions: Has anyone in your family had heart problems at a young age?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Chest Pain Guideline (Gulati et al., Circulation 2021;144:e368-e454), Sec 2.1 supportive text (e377)
items.guideline_quote: A detailed assessment of cardiovascular risk factors, review of systems, past medical history, and family and social history should complement the assessment of presenting symptoms.
